public_rationale: The ordinary reading—a recurring weakness on unusual inputs—is supported. The July 2024 reasoning study documents repeated failures on simple problems and substantial sensitivity to small variations. This does not establish that unfamiliar inputs generally defeat every approach. The materials study supplies an important boundary: many apparently novel tasks succeed, especially when their representations remain covered by training data. The outcome depends on reading 'often' as recurrent failures on relevant tests, not a quantified rate across all AI use.
limitations: The decisive reasoning study is a preprint using a deliberately selected challenge problem.
The evidence does not establish a deployment-wide failure rate.
Exact experimental run dates are not supplied; the 2024 evaluations were public before the post.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Current machine learning approaches handle outliers poorly and often say or do absurd things in unusual circumstances.

statement.excerpt: The simple fact is that current approaches to machine learning (which underlies most of the AI people talk about today) are lousy at outliers, which is to say that when they encounter unusual circumstances, like the subtly altered word problems that I mentioned a few days ago, they often say and do things that are absurd.
statement.document_title: This one important fact about current AI explains almost everything

from_speaker: often say and do things that are absurd
our_interpretation: The plain reading is a recurring reliability weakness on unusual inputs, including plainly incorrect answers to simple altered problems. It does not require every model to fail on every unfamiliar input.
No reporting period is specified. I use 2024 through the post date as the current research period, because model evaluations have no regular quarterly reporting cycle.
Controlled input variations are evidence of robustness problems, but do not by themselves prove that an example was absent from proprietary training data.
Often is assessed as repeated failure across trials and models on relevant challenge sets, not as a measured share of all real-world AI use.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous evaluations show repeated, substantial failures across multiple models on unusual or modestly altered inputs, including plainly incorrect reasoning on otherwise simple tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, well-controlled evaluations show that contemporary approaches reliably handle the relevant unusual inputs, with alleged failures confined to isolated or invalid examples.

evidence.excerpt: AIW reveals severe reasoning deficits in SOTA LLMs.
evidence.locator: Section 3.1, opening statement and accompanying results
evidence.explanation: Repeated tests of a simple family-relation problem found very low success for many models and large fluctuations under small variations. GPT-4 and Claude 3 Opus performed better than most models, so the result supports recurring failures rather than universal inability.

evidence.excerpt: unlikely to achieve high OOD robustness
evidence.explanation: The benchmark reports extensive vision-model weaknesses under distribution shifts. Its original results predate the selected period, and adversarial robustness is narrower than the full claim, so it supplies context only.

Materials-model evaluations found many successful tasks involving withheld chemistry or symmetry. The paper also links poor results to test inputs outside the represented training domain, showing why unfamiliarity alone does not establish likely failure.
